title: Machine-learning screening identifies natural RORγt inhibitors with preclinical psoriasis activity
summary: An ensemble machine-learning screen of natural products prioritized protoberberine alkaloids as candidate RORγt inhibitors. In vitro assays found that berberine and coptisine inhibited Th17 differentiation and directly bound RORγt by surface plasmon resonance; coptisine also showed efficacy in a preclinical mouse psoriasis model.
ai_technology: Ensemble machine-learning models for natural-product RORγt activity and counter-screening, combining graph neural networks and molecular-fingerprint random forests
organization: Bionsight; Incheon National University; Seoul National University; Kangwon National University; Ajou University; Wright State University

evidence.tested: In vitro assays found that berberine and coptisine inhibited Th17 differentiation and directly bound RORγt by surface plasmon resonance; coptisine also showed efficacy in a preclinical mouse psoriasis model.
evidence.unknown: Berberine and coptisine are known natural products; the novelty is their prioritization and experimental characterization as RORγt inhibitors in this workflow, not discovery of new chemical entities. The mouse result is preclinical and does not establish psoriasis treatment in humans. The catalog already contains an unrelated RORγt result involving topotecan; this paper's compounds and evidence are distinct.
evidence.ai_role: Ensemble models screened a natural-product library and prioritized predicted RORγt inhibitors. Chemotaxonomic analysis narrowed candidates to protoberberines; six were experimentally evaluated, and berberine/coptisine showed in-vitro effects and direct target binding, with coptisine tested in a mouse psoriasis model.
